programme.title: Heilstätten
programme.desc: Für den Adrenalinkick wollen sechs Videoblogger in einer verfallenen Klinik unweit von Berlin übernachten. Bewaffnet mit Kameras erhoffen sich die aufgekratzten YouTube-Sternchen „spuktakuläre“ Aufnahmen für viele Klicks. Die Warnung von Schulfreund Theo (Tim Oliver Schultz, „Club der roten Bänder“), hier hätten einst Nazi-Experimente stattgefunden, ignorieren sie. Theos Ex Marnie (Sonja Gerhardt) warnt vor der ermordeten Patientin 106, die hier noch immer ihr Unwesen treiben soll. Da verschwindet plötzlich die Beauty-Bloggerin Betty (Nilam Farooq)…Der Found-Footage-Schocker basiert auf den Mythen rund um das 1898 erbaute Lungensanatorium Beelitz. Um Gruseltourismus zu vermeiden, wurde aber woanders gedreht. Nette Idee, doch an der Umsetzung und den jugendsprachlichen Dialogen hakt es gehörig.

programme.title: Nur Anfänger heiraten
programme.desc: Die kulleräugige Nina (Muriel Baumeister) erbt einen alten Gasthof – und damit auch so einige Sorgen. Ein protziges Romantikhotel nebenan droht ihrem runtergekommenen Betrieb das Wasser abzugraben, und die verwirrte Oma hält sie Tag und Nacht auf Trab. Da klopft Karin an die Tür. Die Fernsehzicke, die sich irrigerweise im Konkurrenz-Hotel wähnt, bittet Nina, ihre große Hochzeit auszurichten. Die Rettung! Nina macht sich mit Feuereifer ans Werk. Bis sie auf den Bräutigam in spe (Benjamin Sadler) trifft…\r\nRegisseurin Meyer Price verlegt die Idee des „J.Lo“- Kinohits „Wedding Planner – Verliebt, verlobt, verplant“ in die deutsche Provinz. Klaro, ist hier alles kleiner und braver, dafür aber auch irgendwie netter. Romantiker dürfen sich auf einen kinoreifen Kuss freuen. \r\n.

programme.title: K11 – Die neuen Fälle
programme.desc: Dokumentarisch, authentisch und hautnah liefert "K11 – Die neuen Fälle" spannende und emotionale Crime-Storys. Die Tatmotive bei Gewaltverbrechen sind oftmals vielschichtig und die Täter gewieft. Trotzdem nehmen die Ermittler tagtäglich den Kampf gegen das Verbrechen auf. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mediashop – Weil es besser geht
programme.desc: "MediaShop" bietet qualitativ hochwertige Produkte, die den Alltag erleichtern, zu einem attraktiven Preis. Nach dem Motto "Weil es besser geht" gibt es bei "MediaShop" Innovationen aus aller Welt und ein unterhaltsames Einkaufserlebnis. Das umfassende Produktportfolio beinhaltet die neuesten Produkte aus den Bereichen Küche, Haushalt, Freizeit, Fitness, Wellness und Beauty. "MediaShop" vertreibt die originalen "As seen on TV" Produkte an Millionen zufriedene Kunden. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Anna und die Liebe
programme.desc: Anna ist Gerrits neue Geheimwaffe. Er nimmt sie gegen alle Vorwürfe von Jonas in Schutz und spricht ihr nachdrücklich das Vertrauen aus, aber glücklich wird Anna bei ihm trotzdem nicht. Sie liebt Jonas, auch wenn er sie schon zu oft beleidigt hat. Aber gegen Katja ist noch kein Kraut gewachsen und solange er ihr vertraut, wird sich das Bild, das er von Anna hat, nicht ändern. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Die Landarztpraxis
programme.desc: Vicki ist tief getroffen, als Simon ihr nicht versprechen kann, ihr Vertrauen niemals wieder zu verletzen. Traurig nimmt sie daraufhin Abschied von ihren Freunden und ihrer Familie und verlässt Wiesenkirchen. In dem Moment erkennt Simon, dass er einen großen Fehler gemacht hat. Er fährt Vicki hinterher, um sie aufzuhalten – doch er findet nur ihren verunglückten Wagen. Von ihr selbst fehlt jede Spur. Wird Simon Vicki rechtzeitig im Wald finden, um ihr das Leben zu retten? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Charmed – Zauberhafte Hexen
programme.desc: Nachdem Gideon die Parallelwelt mit der Normalwelt vermischt hat, ist das Gleichgewicht der Welten aus den Angeln gehoben. Es wird nicht mehr dunkel, kleinste Vergehen werden sofort bestraft. Gideon hat sich zu Barbas, dem Dämon der Angst, in die Unterwelt geflüchtet. Zusammen planen die beiden einen Anschlag auf Wyatt. Er tötet Chris und entführt Wyatt in die Unterwelt. Leo, der seine beiden Söhne an Gideon verloren hat, schwört blutige Rache ... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Charmed – Zauberhafte Hexen
programme.desc: Nachdem Barbas und Gideon versucht haben, Wyatt zu töten, ist Leo außer sich vor Zorn. Blind vor Wut, beginnt er sogar dem Ältestenrat zu misstrauen. Allerdings ahnt er nicht, dass Barbas der Grund für seinen unsagbaren Zorn ist, denn er hat sich Leos Gedanken bemächtigt. Mithilfe von Leos blutigem Rachefeldzug will der Dämon die Ältesten vernichten. Indes sucht Paige nach einer Lösung, um die Zauberschule nach Gideons Tod weiterlaufen zu lassen ... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Charmed – Zauberhafte Hexen
programme.desc: Nach Gideons Tod regiert das Chaos auf der Zauberschule. Als ein Schüler die Frauenrechtlerin Lady Godiva aus dem Mittelalter in die Schule zaubert, kommt unbemerkt der böse Lord Dyson mit in die Gegenwart. Er will Lady Godiva töten. Doch wenn ihm das gelingt, wird die Geschichte verändert, und Frauen werden keine Rechte mehr haben. Indes protestiert Phoebe, inspiriert von Lady Godiva, für die Rechte der Frauen, indem sie nackt auf einem Pferd durch die Stadt reitet ... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Charmed – Zauberhafte Hexen
programme.desc: Chris' Hexentaufe steht bevor, und die gesamte Halliwell-Familie hat sich eingefunden. Damit Wyatt und Chris nicht streiten, belegt Grandma sie mit einem Rivalitätszauber. Doch der Zauber springt auf die Schwestern über und sie verwandeln sich in Teenager. Wenn sie nicht schnellstens wieder "entzaubert" werden, schweben alle in großer Gefahr, denn der Zauber hat auch die Macht der Drei außer Kraft gesetzt. Indes versucht ein mysteriöser Maskendämon, Wyatt zu entführen ... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Desperate Housewives
programme.desc: Lynette erlebt mit, dass sich Eddie nicht beherrschen kann, wenn er wütend wird, und geht mit ihm zu einem Therapeuten. Der möchte aber auch gern Eddies Mutter dazuholen ... Bree entdeckt, dass Sam sie belogen hat, als sie seine Mutter kennenlernt. Als sie Sam daraufhin anspricht, lernt sie eine neue Seite an ihm kennen ... Gabrielle erfährt von Carlos' Geschäftsführer, dass er Mike 50.000 Dollar geliehen hat. Wenig später erzählt sie das der nichtsahnenden Susan ... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Desperate Housewives
programme.desc: Bree versucht, Sam loszuwerden, doch der will nicht gehen. Auf Brees indirekte Drohung reagiert er mit einer Gegendrohung und verlangt, dass Brees Unternehmen auf ihn überschrieben wird. Patrick hat sich bei Angie einquartiert und zwingt sie, eine Bombe zu bauen. Auch Danny hat er nach Hause zurückgelockt. Als Gabrielle kommt und Angie um ein Rezept bittet, versucht Angie, ihr eine Botschaft zu übermitteln. Irinas Leiche wird gefunden – Preston wird von der Polizei befragt. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Garagengold
programme.desc: Lamborghini-Legenden - Die Supersportler von Harald SkjoldtHarald Skjøldt ist der größte Lamborghini-Sammler in Norwegen. Unter anderem nennt er einen 74er Countach sein Eigen, der einmal Frank Sinatra gehörte. Man trifft Harald mit seinen Autos bei zahlreichen Veranstaltungen.

programme.title: Rückwärtsgang
programme.desc: Renault 5Früher war nicht alles besser, aber anders! Kleinwagen, Mittelklasse, Luxusklasse, oder Sportwagen: Wie Autos aus vergangenen Epochen fahren, was sie damals wie heute auszeichnet und wie viel Spaß sie machen, das wird aufgezeigt.

programme.title: Petrolheads
programme.desc: Sportwagen mit königlichem Vorbesitz: Ferrari 275 GTSLeidenschaftliche Oldtimersammler öffnen ihre Garagen und präsentieren ihre besten Schätze. Dabei besprechen sie auch die Geschichte der Autos, ihre persönlichen Verbindungen zu ihnen und die handwerklichen Meisterleistungen hinter den Maschinen.

programme.title: Die Tester KLASSIK
programme.desc: BMW 440i Gran Coupé xDrive vs. KIA Stinger 3.3 T-GDI V6 GTHeute treten der BMW 440i Gran Coupé xDrive und der KIA Stinger 3.3 T-GDI V6 GT im Vergleich an und werden darauf untersucht, ob sie halten, was die Hersteller versprechen. Stärken und Schwächen werden entdeckt, denn sie prüfen auf Herz und Nieren.

programme.title: 100 Meilen

programme.title: 100 Meilen

programme.title: Geniale Exoten: Audi A2
programme.desc: Der Audi A2 ist ein Kleinwagen mit Alukarosserie und nur drei Litern Verbrauch. 1999 stellt Audi diesen technischen Meilenstein auf die Räder. Doch das Modell scheitert am Markt. Die geringen Verkaufszahlen machen den A2 zu einem genialen Exoten.

programme.title: Vorfahrt Mercedes-Benz EQXX
programme.desc: Die Sendung stellt das derzeit vielleicht beste Elektroauto vor, den Mercedes-Benz EQXX.

programme.title: Porsche Sixt Carrera Cup 2026
programme.desc: Porsche Sixt Carrera Cup 2026: Hockenheimring (09.-11.10.2026) Über 30 Jahre Tradition - und heute dynamischer denn je! Der Porsche Sixt Carrera Cup Deutschland zählt zu den prestigeträchtigsten Markenpokalen Europas. Jahr für Jahr misst sich hier ein extrem starkes Starterfeld, aus dem zahlreiche Champions den Sprung an die Spitze des Motorsports geschafft haben. Doch dieser Cup ist weit mehr als nur ein Karrieresprungbrett - er ist eine echte Bewährungsprobe für Fahrer, die sich der ultimativen Herausforderung stellen wollen.

programme.title: Fast Lap
programme.desc: Audi RS 4Ein Auto - ein Rennfahrer - eine Runde: Christian Menzel unterzieht den Audi RS 4 dem ultimativen Praxistest. Wer schafft die Runde am schnellsten? Ein Kampf gegen die Zeit.

programme.title: Fast Lap
programme.desc: Porsche 718 Cayman GTSPorsche bläst mit seinem neuen Cayman GTS zum Angriff gegen die Konkurrenz. Der Porsche 718 Cayman GTS wird von Rennfahrer Christian Menzel getestet. Der Cayman GTS kommt mit 4-Zylinder-Boxer und des Weiteren ist er 365 PS stark.

programme.title: Menzel fährt
programme.desc: Mercedes-AMG GT Black SeriesDer Motorsport-Profi Christian Menzel fährt den 730 PS starken Mercedes-AMG GT Black Series.

programme.title: Moove - Mobilität von morgen
programme.desc: e.Volution Street ScooterMobilität ist mehr, als nur mit dem Auto von A nach B zu fahren. Gerade im urbanen Umfeld müssen neue Wege gefunden werden, um nachhaltige Mobilität zu sichern und die Verkehrswende voranzutreiben.

programme.title: Der E-Auto Supertest
programme.desc: E27 — Top oder Flop? Der Ford Elektro-Explorer im E-Auto-SupertestOb Kleinwagen, Luxuslimousine oder SUV. Die neusten E-Autos müssen sich im Supertest beweisen. Alexander Bloch testet alle Stromer ausführlich und vergibt pro Kategorie maximal sechs Sterne. Welches Modell schafft es im Gesamtranking nach ganz oben.

programme.desc: S1 E10 — SchadensbegrenzungNachdem ET das Schiff von Galvin Daley repariert hat und mit seinen Kindern die Fahrt fortsetzt, stellt sich heraus, dass es sich nicht um einen Familienausflug, sondern um Kindesentführung handelt. Die Crew nimmt die Verfolgung auf, Galvin flüchtet jedoch in die Mangroven. Dort lauert jedoch in der Dunkelheit eine tödliche Gefahr: Krokodile greifen nicht nur Galvin und seine Kinder an.

programme.title: Sea Patrol
programme.desc: S1 E11 — BlutdiamantenAls die Crew der Hammersley die Passagiere eines sinkenden Schiffes an Bord nimmt, überwältigt einer der Männer Swain und nimmt ihn als Geisel. Mit dem Beiboot der Hammersley fahren sie mit dem gefesselten Swain zum sinkenden Schiff, um die brisante Ladung zu bergen. Die Crew der Hammersley muss behutsam vorgehen, um das Leben ihres Kollegen bei der Befreiungsaktion nicht zu gefährden.

programme.title: Sea Patrol
programme.desc: S1 E12 — In letzter SekundeSwain und seine Frau sind gerade im Kreißsaal und erwarten die Geburt ihres Kindes, während Swain kurzfristig auf die Hammersley kommandiert wird. Schweren Herzens lässt er seine Frau zurück, um mit seinem Team einem Hilferuf entgegen zu schippern. Simon und seiner hochschwangeren Freundin ist das Benzin ausgegangen und die Wehen setzen ein. Zeitgleich gilt es einen Giftmordanschlag zu vereiteln.

programme.title: Sea Patrol
programme.desc: S1 E13 — Die letzte FahrtDie letzte Fahrt der Hammersley fordert noch einmal alles von ihrer Crew: Zusammen mit der Polizei soll mithilfe von Ursula der kriminelle Gallagher dingfest gemacht werden. Er nimmt gerade Kurs auf indonesische Hoheitsgewässer, um dort todbringendes Gift auf dem Schwarzmarkt zu verkaufen. Ursula, die undercover auf Gallaghers Schiff einen Peilsender platzieren soll, gerät zwischen die Fronten.

programme.desc: Der kürzlich im Kampf gefallene Soldat Ray Garrison erhält eine zweite Chance, als ein Unternehmen ihn von den Toten auferstehen lässt. Mit Nanotechnologie in seinen Adern entwickelt er eine unaufhaltsame Kraft und hat außerdem die Fähigkeit zur sofortigen Selbstheilung. Als das Unternehmen jedoch beginnt, seinen Geist und seine Erinnerungen zu manipulieren, muss Garrison sich auf eine verzweifelte Mission begeben, um herauszufinden, was real ist und was nicht.

programme.title: Sea Patrol

Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: What makes sharks built for speed? How do snakes move without limbs? How do sugar gliders fly without feathers? The answer all lies in their skin. Professor Ben Garrod uncovers the secrets of how skin has evolved to enable animals to solve some of the most remarkable challenges on Earth. To do this, Ben heads to the specialist flight centre at the Royal Veterinary College to analyse the way a sugar glider uses its skin flaps to stay aloft. He goes diving with sharks at the Blue Planet Aquarium and discovers that, far from being smooth, sharkskin is incredibly rough. It is covered with thousands of tiny teeth that make a shark hydrodynamic. Ben also finds out how the keratinised scales on snakes' bellies are the perfect configuration to allow them to move over virtually any surface they encounter. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Gareth Edwards's Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Gareth and Maureen Edwards head to St Davids, a place which holds half a lifetime of special memories for them. After making 53 appearances for Wales, Gareth retired from rugby in 1978. After years in the public eye, he and Maureen booked a holiday in St Davids for them and their young boys. The holiday was such a hit, they returned every summer for more than 40 years. Gareth and Maureen begin with a visit to a shire horse farm. A century ago there were more than a million shire horses in the UK, but today there are under 3,000 and the farm is working to safeguard the species. Gareth and Maureen meet the horses before finding out who can master driving a shire horse-drawn carriage. Later, watching the St Davids rugby team train on the beach brings back memories for Gareth who, as a young player, did the same with the Welsh team at Aberavon beach. The couple are delighted to catch up with old friend, Dai Chant, the medal-winning former coxswain of the St Davids' lifeboat. The old lifeboat station he worked from has been abandoned in favour of a state-of-the-art station next door. They see the new lifeboat launch as the crew go out on exercise. Catching a boat to Ramsey Island, Gareth and Maureen visit the remote bird sanctuary and discover the colony of razorbills – or "razorblades" as Maureen call them – on the precipitous wild cliffs on the far side of the island. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In the last of the series, archaeologist and historian Richard Miles examines the rise and fall of the Roman Empire. At the height of its power, the Roman Empire extended the benefits of its civilization to a 60 million citizens and subjects in a swathe of territory that extended from Hadrian's Wall to the banks of the Euphrates. Even under the rule of mad, bad and dangerous emperors, the imperial system proved to be robust, buttressed by the support of elite families in the far-flung corners of the empire whose loyalty was ensured by a system of cultural aspiration, economic opportunity and military coercion. But the material benefits of the "good order" delivered by Roman rule provided its citizens and subjects with the security to ask profound questions about the meaning of life, questions that the pragmatic, polytheistic Roman belief system was ill-equipped to answer. Christianity grew to fill the spiritual vacuum at the heart of Roman civilization, eventually claiming an Emperor, Constantine, as its greatest prize. The City of Man would be eclipsed the City of God. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: UK history professor Robert Bartlett gives you a crash course in Norse history, outlining some of the most significant Norse (Viking) leaders. Robert travels across the British Isles, to Jerusalem over to Italy, exploring the extent of Norse influence between the 10th and 13th century. Watch as the professor visit historical landmarks and examine artefacts in relation to the greatest Norse conquerors, including Rollo, his successor Duke William the Bastard, and more. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: How does a giraffe stay cool? What are different porcupine quills teaching us about medicine? What makes some people more likely to be bitten by mosquitoes than others? All the answers and more lie in the secrets of how skin protects us from a hostile world. When it comes to protecting our delicate insides, skin is like an external suit of armour. Animals have adapted ways of protecting themselves from everything a hostile planet has to throw at them. Hippos produce their own sunscreen to protect themselves against the dangers of UV rays from the sun. Only recently discovered by science, is the truth behind a giraffe's spots, a network of blood vessels that they use to cool themselves down in the blazing heat of the African savannah. Professor Ben Garrod discovers how. He tests the limitations of human skin by plunging himself into a deep freezer to demonstrate how human skin just isn't well insulated enough to cope with extreme cold. He discovers how human skin is an entire ecosystem for bugs and bacteria as he comes face to face with what is growing on his skin. And he gets bitten by mosquitoes and stable flies as he learns that disease-carrying insects have evolved to pierce everything from human skin to horse hide. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Gareth Edwards's Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: For the last of their new adventures, Maureen has arranged a trip to the spectacular Brecon Beacons. But it's not the usual walks amid epic mountain scenery on the agenda. In a first for both, the childhood sweethearts enlist in tank school. After donning cam cream and military gear, the couple get a lesson in controlling a full-sized tank. Maureen's keen to see if the new vehicle can pick up speed. Their accommodation is another new experience – a shepherd's hut complete with lush rolling hills for a view and sheep for neighbours. Gareth is a keen clay pigeon shooter and wants Maureen to try her hand at the sport. After getting some tips from farmer and Welsh champion clay shooter Rhys Lewis, the competitive pair are both determined not to be the one to miss. Meanwhile, Gareth and Maureen's inability to take one in-focus photograph of their adventures continues. Photographer Rhian Mai meets them at a spectacular natural cave to help hone their skills. The weekend ends where the original adventure began – on one of Wales's most beautiful canals. Hopes start high as, with a little help, they manage to stay on course and not crash. But it isn't long before the barge runs aground and the battle resumes to determine who was responsible. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: How the Romans Conquered the Alps
The Planets
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox continues his exploration of the solar system with a visit to a planet that dwarfs all the others: Jupiter. Its enormous size gives it a great power that it has used to manipulate the other planets – a power both for good and bad that it wields to this day. Jupiter is not only the biggest but also the oldest planet in the solar system. It alone witnessed the birth of the Sun and ever since its immense gravity has shaped the destiny of the other worlds. Soon after its birth, its orbit shifted inwards bringing it ever closer to the sun. As it moved, it created chaos in the the region of space that would become the asteroid belt, ensuring that no planet could form here, only a tiny failed planet Ceres, which remains today. As it continued into the inner solar system, Jupiter used its power to throw raw material needed to form planets into the Sun, stunting the growth of Mars, a planet that might otherwise have grown as large as Earth. Indeed, Jupiter would have obliterated every last rocky world on its journey into the Sun, if a tussle with another giant – Saturn – had not brought it back from the brink. Today Jupiter's great mass continues to be felt. Its gravity torments its moon Io, creating the most volcanically active body in the solar system. And through the vice-like grip it exerts over the asteroid belt, Jupiter's influence extends as far as Earth – where it retains the power to change the course of life on our planet. And where, as Brian reveals, it might even have created the conditions for humanity to inherit the Earth. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Timewatch
programme.desc: Documentary that re-examines the attempt to blow up the Houses of Parliament in 1605 – one of the most famous yet least understood events in British history. It shows how the plot was almost England's 9/11, and asks why a group of young Englishmen became so radicalised and so hell-bent on terrorism. Computer graphics recreate what the Houses of Parliament looked like in 1605, and show just how close the plotters came to success. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Planets
programme.desc: Join Professor Brian Cox as he explores the planets of our solar system in this fascinating and stunning, five-part documentary series. Brian traces our knowledge as a species of these giant, celestial bodies, examining each planet's story and makeup. He looks back at their existence over billions of years, revealing each planet's journey with dazzling cinematography and compelling detail. Whether it's the gargantuan size of Jupiter, the mysterious history of Saturn or the complexion of the four inner most planets, this series is informative and beautiful in equal measure. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Battlefield Britain
programme.desc: In the last episode in this series, Dan Snow experiences for himself how the Battle of Britain was fought at the limits of human endurance when he takes flight in a high performance stunt plane. Recreating the spiralling turns of a dogfight, he feels the extraordinary side-effects of the high G forces felt by pilots in this critical battle of WWII. Using revolutionary graphics, Peter Snow gives a blow-by-blow account of the pivotal moments of the battle and how the RAF held off the might of the German Luftwaffe during the summer of 1940. The future of the entire country was at stake in this, the first great air battle in history. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Guns of Navarone
programme.desc:
November 1943: Von der Insel Keros können 2000 britische Soldaten nicht evakuiert werden, da der einzige Zugang zum Meer von zwei riesigen Kanonen der Deutschen auf der Insel Navarone bewacht wird. 

Ein eilig zusammengestelltes Kommandounternehmen aus kriegserfahrenen Freiwilligen soll helfen: darunter Captain Mallory (Gregory Peck), ein neuseeländischer Bergsteiger, der britische Sprengstoffexperte Miller (David Niven) und der griechische Offizier Stavros (Anthony Quinn). Der Plan sieht vor, an Soldaten und Spionen vorbei die Felsen zu erklimmen und die Geschütze zu zerstören…

Mit großem Staraufgebot und viel Action errang das genreprägende Kriegsepos sieben Oscar-Nominierungen, darunter für den Besten Film. Es gab dann einen für die Effekte.

programme.title: Halloween
programme.desc: Wenn Amerika die Nacht der ausgehöhlten Kürbisse feiert und die Kinder in Skelett-Kostümen die Erwachsenen erschrecken, dann ist Halloween. John Carpenter („Die Klapperschlange“) macht aus dem Verkleidungsspiel schrecklichen Ernst: An jenem Tag bricht der Psychopath Michael Myers aus einer psychiatrischen Anstalt aus, um in seiner Heimat Illinois, wo er als Sechsjähriger seine Killerkarriere begann, ein Blutbad anzurichten. Er nimmt die schüchterne Babysitterin Laurie (Jamie Lee Curtis) und ihre liebestollen Kicher-Freundinnen ins Visier…\n\nDer voll Suspense-Spannung steckende Low-Budget-Thriller gab den Startschuss für eine Flut von Horrorfilmen, in denen sexhungrige Teenager dezimiert werden (wie z. B. „Scream“).

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: On the night of Christmas 1998, a homeless man enters the infamous Greyfriars Kirkyard in Edinburgh. Seeking refuge, he broke into the tomb of George Mackenzie – Edinburgh's famous executioner – then fell into an assembly of decomposing corpses. His screams were heard above ground, but something else had been disturbed. Within weeks, stories of blackouts and inexplicable attacks began to spread. The injuries were so severe that Edinburgh City Council locked the gates and declared the area out of bounds for public safety. Jan Andrew Henderson began to chronicle the Mackenzie Poltergeist – only to claim to become a target of its malice. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Hauntings
programme.desc: In 1958, two young women travel together in a Ford Sedan to a nightclub in Georgia, on the other side of Lake Lanier. But they never return. Weeks later, reports begin of a ghostly figure: a lady wearing a blue dress, walking across the lake, whilst calls for help are heard from the waters below. Then, stories of unexplained drownings emerge. Mysterious deaths at Lake Lanier abound, whilst survivors report the feeling of being pulled into the depths or held beneath by unseen hands. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Weather For the Week Ahead
programme.desc: Detailed weather report. Bringing you details of current weather conditions for across the UK and what to expect for the next seven days. With forecasts, temperatures and weather warnings. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC,which is designed to inform you on current affairs. The BBC is aims to be a totally impartial public service broadcaster, and was established by Royal Charter. The BBC is funded by a licence fee paid by British households, and is regulated by Ofcom. They aim to create high-quality content, in order to inform and educate, but also entertain, their audience Millions of people from all over the world watch content produced by the BBC, and they are well respected as a media company. It was founded in 1922, with its headquarters in Westminster, London. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: BBC One's flagship morning current affairs programme with news headlines and regular weather reports. Start your day with the biggest national and international stories. Breakfast takes a look at the day's papers and brings you the latest developments in sports, politics, business and entertainment. Breakfast welcomes guests to the studio for a chat. Whilst analysis and special reports offer a greater understanding of important subjects. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Learn the tricks of the trade when you go to the auctions with Homes Under the Hammer. Join presenters Martin Roberts, Dion Dublin and Martel Maxwell as they follow the renovation stories of properties across Britain as they get transformed from empty shells and outdated buildings to desirable spaces and contemporary homes. Watch as ordinary people breathe new life into the otherwise unloved houses, and find out how well they managed to stay within budget. Will they sell and make a profit, or have they invested too much money in a project that wont sell? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Join Charlie Ross for today's Bargain Hunt as he heads to Builth Wells in mid-Wales. With the expert help of Kate Bliss and Tim Weeks, the reds and the blues battle it out at the Royal Welsh Showground in Powys to see who can buy the most profitable three items to take to auction. Charlie heads off to visit a grand hall built in the early 1880s. It's now a museum but was once the local courtroom with accommodation for the judge-in-residence, all under one roof. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: Early afternoon round-up of the day's biggest national and international stories. The BBC News Team bring you the headlines and essential up-to-the-minute information about the latest developments. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Sarah Moore sifts through bootfuls of rubbish at Beaconsfield recycling centre in the hope of finding three gems amongst the junk. Lighting designer Duncan McKean takes on a pair of mirrors and a lacrosse stick, and a wrought-iron stand tests the creative mettle of blacksmiths Bex Simon and Dave Harris. Sarah sets to work updating a reproduction desk, but will she succeed in producing profits from all three items? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Push factors from the noisy, bustling cities of Britain, combined with the alluring peace of the countryside, has the population dreaming of homes in more scenic surroundings. Escape to the Country sees buyers from different areas on the UK considering their options to settle down in the English countryside. Presenters show off a range of prospective homes, before they must make their final decision towards the end of the show. Each episode taking place in a different region of the UK, we see a wide variety of beautiful homes across the country. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Interesting docu-reality show, hosted by English actor and presenter Nigel Havers, in which a panel of dealers provide expert advice and buy off various antique and collectable items brought in by members of the public. Nigel welcomes people who have intriguing, often peculiar and extraordinary items they want to sell- anything from toys and furniture to musical instruments, and introduces them to an expert who provides them with some information about the object. Sellers then go to the ''Bidding room'' where they meet five dealers who have to bid against each other if they want to take home these incredible items. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Fortune, Xav, Nellie and Kaân – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The high pressure game show, where pointless answers are the way to win. Contestants not only have to answer questions correctly, but give the answer that scores the least points. They do this by coming up with the least obvious answers, that other people struggle to come up with in a survey of individuals. A correct answer that nobody else managed to say is a pointless answer, the best possible outcome. A pointless answer in the final round is how you win the jackpot, cash prize, which grows with every episode until someone wins. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest news from the BBC,which is designed to inform you on current affairs. The BBC is aims to be a totally impartial public service broadcaster, and was established by Royal Charter. The BBC is funded by a licence fee paid by British households, and is regulated by Ofcom. They aim to create high-quality content, in order to inform and educate, but also entertain, their audience Millions of people from all over the world watch content produced by the BBC, and they are well respected as a media company. It was founded in 1922, with its headquarters in Westminster, London. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: A show with big-name guests and special reports on a range of subjects including consumer rights, current affairs and contemporary issues. The One Show looks at topics from the quirky and rare to much more serious matters. Since first hitting British screens in 2006, The One Show has welcomed hundreds of celebrities to its sofa. With high-profile from stage, screen, sport, music, politics and more; including then-British-Prime Minister Theresa May, Daniel Radcliffe, Dame Judy Dench, Sir Tom Jones and many, many more. With fun, laughs and the occasional musical number. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: EastEnders is a series set in Albert Square in the East End of London in the fictional Borough of Walford. Here respectable townhouses are next to offices and apartments. We follow everyday stories of local residents and their families. The locals live their ordinary lives- go to night clubs, markets, pubs and cafes. They fall in love and fight, get sick, get divorced. Kids can break a window, neighbors can pick a fight. There is nothing extraordinary but life in the East End is full of various moments of fun. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure – a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia. Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre. Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that's as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day. Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia. The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet – traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia. Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people. First-time backpackers Princess and Junior have shared a childhood in the public eye, making their sibling bond incredibly strong, but find themselves in at the deep end when trying to navigate the winding streets of the Sarawak capital. Keen to make the most of the adventure, they choose to spend time in Malaysia, putting in a shift at a family-run coconut farm in Mount Kuwai. Ella and best friend Nana bonded at school but now live countries apart. Hoping the race will reunite them, they embrace village life in West Kalimantan and are welcomed into a traditional Dayak longhouse. But with erratic public transport running through the remote rainforest, the pair face a nerve-racking dilemma. Determined to keep up with the youngest of the teams but the most cautious of the pairs, Jeff and his son Matt face an early test to their relationship as they get off to a faltering start. They manage to escape the intense equatorial heat by opting for water travel down the coast through the meandering river delta. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones – Nessa from Gavin and Stacey – investigates her Welsh family's history. programme.title: Film: The Monkey (2025)
programme.desc:
Panisch versucht Petey Shelburn, in einem Antiquitätenladen ein Aufziehäffchen loszuwerden. Kurz darauf ist der Ladenbesitzer ausgeweidet und Petey verschwunden. Seine Söhne, die Zwillinge Hal und Bill, finden den Affen und stellen fest, dass immer, wenn sie ihn aufziehen, kurz darauf jemand grausam zu Tode kommt. Sie zerstören das Spielzeug und werfen es in einen Brunnen. Doch 25 Jahre später kommt es in ihrem Umfeld erneut zu mysteriösen Todesfällen. Der Affe muss zurück sein – und irgendjemand verwendet seine Kräfte… 

Die äußerst elaborierten, durch den Affen beschworenen Zufälle, durch die hier Menschen sterben, erinnern an die besten Szenen der „Final Destination“-Reihe. Regisseur Oz Perkins macht sich einen plumpen Splatter-Spaß aus dem Umbringen seiner Figuren, will aber zugleich auch eine ernste Allegorie auf abwesende Väter und die Auswirkungen auf deren Söhne erzählen. 

Das geht tonal nicht immer auf und strauchelt manchmal gewaltig, gleichzeitig inszeniert Perkins jedoch so derbe und kreativ ausufernd, dass man seinem Skript einige Patzer verzeiht. Großartig ist der ungemein gruselige Affe selbst, der trotz seines starren Blicks einen ganz eigenen Charakter entwickelt und sich richtig schön hassen lässt. Eine Schauermär wie einst aus der Twilight Zone.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Young Benjamin's got an eye for a bargain, Kevin's hoping the dealers deliver on his Pashley bike, and will font-of-all-knowledge Peter sell off an intriguing family heirloom? Making a beeline for the bidders today is Benjamin from Leeds. He's brought a Balinese Ubud painting picked up in a local charity shop. Will his exotic artwork prove a lucky find? Gloria has come all the way from Forfar to sell her dumb valet. One of the dealers will surely be tempted – if not to sell on, just to keep their many glamorous outfits in ready-to-wear condition. Who will purchase Peter's prize-winning miniature church font, designed many years ago by a family member? It's perfect for the man or woman about town who wants their own ecclesiastical antique but can't quite fit the full-sized thing in at home. This bijou bargain, on the other hand, would even fit in Ian's caravan. Wheeler-dealer Kevin rolls in next, with his iconic Pashley delivery bike. It once belonged to famous listings magazine Time Out, but given his high reserve price, Kevin is in danger of having to cycle it straight back to London. Last before we shut up shop for another day is Jessica from Newcastle, with her trusty steed – a Dala horse. Originally a children's toy, in the 1930s these carved and colourfully painted trinkets gained popularity as souvenirs and are now sought-after, mid-century collectibles. (Senderinfo).

programme.desc: See Hear presenter Lisa Kelly is joined in the studio by Adrian Bailey, former president of CODA International and an interpreter, to explore the experiences of mixed deaf and hearing families, looking at identity, communication, belonging and the importance of sign language. programme.title: Hawaii: Earth's Tropical Islands
programme.desc: This is a journey across Hawaii's varied islands, discovering how they were made and the incredible wildlife that thrives there. Hawaii is the most remote island chain on earth, and its tropical shores are hard to reach. But for the hardy creatures that can make it here, like the waterfall-climbing fish, carnivorous caterpillar and Laysan albatross, a land of opportunity awaits. From newly formed lava fields to lush jungles and vibrant coral reefs, these diverse and beautiful islands have it all. Packed with surprising stories, the hidden gems of this tropical paradise are uncovered using stunning photography. Dramatic footage of the humpback whale heat run – the biggest courtship battle in the world – and intimate views of the world's oldest known bird feeding its chick are just some of the highlights of what Hawaii has to offer. The islands are so isolated that it used to be that one new species arrived every 100,000 years, but the arrival of people has radically changed the face of Hawaii. Now it gains around 20 new species every year. The remarkable Jackson's chameleon is one of the animals recently introduced. Showing off its voracious appetite, the programme reveals how it is eating its way through the native animals and contributing to wiping them out entirely. But this is a place where people are looking to the future and attempting to bring wildlife back from the brink of extinction. White terns, once extinct on the main islands of Hawaii, have gone from a single pair to over 2,000 birds in the last 60 years. It is a huge challenge, but people are seeking progressive new ways to live alongside nature to allow Hawaii's wildlife to continue to thrive. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Vintage Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques valuation programme. A team of well-respected experts travel around the UK visiting a string of beautiful locations such as castles, stately homes, mansions, gardens and museums. They are met by members of the public who have brought along an antique, family heirloom or curio, eager for a current valuation. The experts have their own specialisms and are always on the lookout for a surprise discovery among the artwork, furniture, jewellery, silver, books, clothing and more. The entertainment comes from the conversations about the histories of the more interesting items, and the suspense as the owners and onlookers who gather around the stands await the experts' estimations about how much each would go for at auction. (Senderinfo).

Anita Manning discovers a Victorian dynamometer used for measuring the pressure of steam, and David Harper is taken back to the days of ocean liners with a wine stopper from 1912. Paul Martin visits Cromer to find out about the RNLI's most decorated lifeboatman. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mortimer and Whitehouse: Gone Fishing.
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the River Ribble in Lancashire for one last fish with their little canine pal, Ted. The beautiful river Ribble runs through the rolling hills of the Yorkshire Dales, onwards to Lancashire before meeting the Irish Sea in Lytham. With the river in good health, Paul and Bob hope to catch a good chub or a mighty barbel on this stretch of the water, while Ted hopes to taste Bob's Lancashire hotpot. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry *
programme.desc: Experts claim that artificial intelligence has begun to exhibit early signs of agency. What does the rise of the superintelligence mean for society? Is humanity on a path to superintelligence or hurtling towards self-destruction? Professor Hannah Fry explores the promises and threats of AI, considering the ways in which superintelligent machines could help humanity as well as the ways in which they could be a hindrance. Over the course of the episode, a range of experts discuss the future of humanity in the age of AI. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life: The Best Bits.
Repair Shop
programme.desc: First into the barn is Alistair Waite, with a fragile cake topper from his parents' wedding cake, which holds memories of a childhood spent growing up in the circus. The centrepiece of the miniature circus scene is a faithful reproduction of the big top, of which Alistair's father was the tent manager and where his mother performed each night. Paper restorer Angelina Bakalarou takes on the delicate task of restoring this precious memento, preserving a unique piece of circus heritage and family love. Next in comes former children's TV presenter Jenny Hanley, who brings along a cherished toy of great historical and personal significance: a stuffed monkey named Alphonse. This cheeky primate helped Jenny's grandmother, Lisa Sheridan, take a series of relaxed and intimate portraits of the royal family, most notably of the young Princesses Elizabeth and Margaret. It was Alphonse's job to attract the subject's attention to the camera, but now, threadbare and worn, he's in no condition to turn heads, royal or otherwise. It's down to Bear Ladies Julie and Amanda to weave their magic, and bring him back to peak condition. Londoner Abdul and his daughter Hannah are next through the barn doors, with a challenging proposal for horologist Steve Fletcher and woodworker Will Kirk. Their beautiful but very broken regulator clock was the dearest possession of Abdul's father, who had been gifted it by a much-loved friend. Passed down to Abdul on his father's death, the clock sadly didn't survive the passage from India, and it is now in a pitiful state, leaving Abdul racked with guilt. It takes all of Will and Steve's skills – and the help of a new face in the barn, screen printer Alasdair MacKay – to get this precious heirloom back to its very best. Finally, Maureen Armstrong from Bristol presents a battered helmet from the Second World War era for the close attention of Lucia Scalisi. The helmet belonged to Maureen's much-missed grandmother Dot, who served as a volunteer nurse during the Blitz and wore the helmet on duty as she tended to the wounded during bombing raids on Portsmouth. Now flaking and rust-spattered, Lucia sets to work to ensure that its history – and Dot's name – are preserved for future generations. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Get Out: 90 Days to Escape Amin
programme.desc: In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president – a former boxer and soldier – as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British – with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: The seasons are changing at Longmeadow, and Monty is planting spring-flowering bulbs to provide colour and interest in the months ahead. It's also time to clear the greenhouse to make space for winter storage. Adam Frost visits RHS Harlow Carr to see how the newly renovated borders are flourishing. Arit Anderson talks to members of the Coco Collective, who grow and cook food from their inner-city allotment, and Sue Kent is at home creating a new planting scheme for next spring. In Oxfordshire, grower Andy Howard shares his passion for the heritage apples thriving in his back garden micro nursery. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: Football for All
programme.desc: See Hear celebrates the beautiful game, exploring deaf football, the fight for accessibility and the inspiring people breaking down barriers on and off the pitch. In the studio, presenter Ahmed Mudawi welcomes Oliver Eadsforth, a passionate advocate for deaf football who works with the England and Great Britain teams, supporting players and helping develop the game on and off the pitch. Oliver reflects on his lifelong love of football, from playing goalkeeper at school and university to taking on roles in administration, player development and international football. He discusses the progress made in deaf sport, the importance of having a voice in decision-making and why more opportunities are needed for deaf people to become coaches and leaders. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's exploration of Essex reaches Chelmsford. At a huge construction site on the outskirts of the city he discovers Beaulieu Park, the first railway station to be built on the Great Eastern Main Line for over 100 years. Michael learns how the station is designed to alleviate congestion in Chelmsford city centre. At Chelmsford Cathedral, the headquarters of the diocese of Chelmsford, Michael meets the bishop of Chelmsford, the Rt Revd Dr Guli Francis-Dehqani. He discovers one of the largest and most diverse dioceses in England and hears Bishop Guli's extraordinary personal story of escape from Iran after the Islamic revolution of 1979. Michael continues his rail journey on the Great Eastern Main Line and visits the historic riverside town of Maldon, with its pretty Thames barges. Michael learns about a medieval battle and handles a rare Viking sword. He finishes this leg of his Essex journey in the coastal village of Tollesbury, with its strong maritime heritage and marshy landscape, a haven for birds and wildlife. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Arriving in the Essex market town of Witham, Michael heads into the countryside to visit Terling Place, one of the county's great country houses. He hears how in the late 19th century, Victorian scientist the 3rd Baron Rayleigh discovered the atmospheric gas argon here. Michael joins the Braintree branch line – aka the Flitch line – and alights at Cressing to visit two huge medieval barns that are thought to be the oldest timber-framed structures in England. At Braintree, Michael learns about the town's wool and silk industries before heading to the Warner and Sons archive, where he discovers a depository of thousands of silk patterns, including two pieces with a royal connection. At Great Bardfield, Michael traces a group of artists including Edward Bawden and Eric Ravilious, who settled in the pretty Essex village from the 1930s onwards. He meets the author of a book on the artists, who now lives in their former home. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Secrets of the Aquarium
programme.sub-title: Moving a Shark Is an Adrenaline Rush
programme.desc: Marcus, the new curator, attempts a high-risk move for a problem shark to the top of the aquarium. Andrew builds a cave for a reclusive lobster, and star attraction Friday the turtle suffers a nasty bite from a mystery tankmate. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Vintage Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head to Abergavenny in Wales. Among the items brought to light are a carved whalebone originally given as a love token to be worn in a corset and a macabre pottery model of a famous Victorian murder scene valued at 5,000 pounds. Also, a bizarre coincidence unites two Beatles collectors. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin visits the Watts Gallery in the heart of the Surrey countryside, where experts David Harper and Thomas Plant are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. David uncovers a collection of British film and TV memorabilia and Thomas is thrilled by some French cameo glass. Paul Martin is on the trail of Martians in Woking, the setting for HG Wells's sci-fi novel The War of the Worlds. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: New: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Les Dennis, Jenny Eclair, Owain Wyn Evans and Lauren Patel take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Strictly It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor has all the backstage gossip and behind-the-scenes action from the world of Strictly, and costume designer Vicky Gill has an exclusive look at some of the couples' Halloween outfits ahead of the weekend. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Breast Cancer Scandal: Exposing the Harm.
programme.desc: BBC Health correspondent Sharon Barbour investigates a deepening breast cancer scandal in County Durham. Women describe feeling "mutilated" after discovering mastectomies they were told they needed were in fact unnecessary. As hundreds of cases of patient harm emerge, Sharon challenges the new hospital boss: why were women subjected to life-changing surgery they did not need, and were warnings ignored? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: UEFA Women's Champions League: Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain.
BBC Weather
programme.desc: BBC Weather provides forecast information for locations across UK and the world. Get the latest updates on the weather, know what to expect. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Uncanny
programme.desc: In the final case of the series, Danny is joined in the studio by Angela and her daughter Emily. They tell him about events that happened to them in the early 2000s when Emily was a child. A seemingly supernatural presence that began as what Angela thought was an imaginary friend, soon grew into something far more terrifying. Both Emily and her sister became too scared to sleep in their rooms, supposedly beset by the malign presence of an old man who threatened Emily and her family. When Angela's friends and babysitters began to experience things too, refusing to return to the house, Angela worried for the safety of her daughter. Events escalated to the point where the family felt they were physically in danger. It all seems beyond belief until Danny investigates the history of the house and makes a shocking discovery. As ever, the audience is invited to share their theories and help crack the case. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Experts claim that artificial intelligence has begun to exhibit early signs of agency. What does the rise of the superintelligence mean for society? Is humanity on a path to superintelligence or hurtling towards self-destruction? Professor Hannah Fry explores the promises and threats of AI, considering the ways in which superintelligent machines could help humanity as well as the ways in which they could be a hindrance. Over the course of the episode, a range of experts discuss the future of humanity in the age of AI. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: See Hear: Football for All
programme.desc: See Hear celebrates the beautiful game, exploring deaf football, the fight for accessibility and the inspiring people breaking down barriers on and off the pitch. In the studio, presenter Ahmed Mudawi welcomes Oliver Eadsforth, a passionate advocate for deaf football who works with the England and Great Britain teams, supporting players and helping develop the game on and off the pitch. Oliver reflects on his lifelong love of football, from playing goalkeeper at school and university to taking on roles in administration, player development and international football. He discusses the progress made in deaf sport, the importance of having a voice in decision-making and why more opportunities are needed for deaf people to become coaches and leaders. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion is delighted with the space on offer to play football in Northamptonshire. Martin finds you need to wipe your feet on the way out of a house in Derbyshire. Martel doesn't know where to start with the dilapidation at a Kilmarnock property. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Les Dennis, Jenny Eclair, Owain Wyn Evans and Lauren Patel take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing.
programme.desc: Paul and Bob travel to the River Ribble in Lancashire for one last fish with their little canine pal, Ted. The beautiful river Ribble runs through the rolling hills of the Yorkshire Dales, onwards to Lancashire before meeting the Irish Sea in Lytham. With the river in good health, Paul and Bob hope to catch a good chub or a mighty barbel on this stretch of the water, while Ted hopes to taste Bob's Lancashire hotpot. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Clive Myrie's Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: The Coronation Market is the largest street market in all of Jamaica, and it's nestled in Downtown Kingston. It's where Clive brushes up on his Jamaican patois and tries out some of the best street food on the island. He also catches up with a mural art collective who have been transforming this district before checking out a trendy boutique to get kitted out with some brand new Downtown threads, hoping to look the part for a night out at the hottest reggae club in town. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Coast to Coast Food Festival
programme.desc: Colin Murray and Edith Bowman explore Ballycastle's famous Ould Lammas Fair and find out how Venezuelan street food made it to Northern Ireland. They discover how to make money go further when it comes to meat, and Colin introduces Edith to Yellowman and dulce. Chef Julie Lin digs deep to reveal some myths about frozen food, and food journalist Leyla Kazim joins fishermen off the Cornish coast in search of sardines. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael's exploration of Essex is drawing to a close. He visits Colchester, which was first mentioned in AD 77 and proudly claims to be Britain's oldest recorded town. He learns about the rebellion in AD 60 by the warrior queen Boudica against the Romans and visits the Norman castle that was built on top of the foundations of the Temple of Claudius. At the University of Essex's plant innovation centre, Michael meets scientists growing climate-resistant plants in a state-of-the-art laboratory, where the weather can be changed at will. Across the Chappel viaduct, one the largest in the country, Michael reaches north Essex. He is bound for the Colne Valley heritage railway and learns the history of the line which ran from Chappel and Wakes Colne to Haverhill in Suffolk. He finishes his tour of Essex by driving an old Intercity 125 high-speed train through the picturesque countryside. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Görevimiz Yemek
programme.desc: İki gurme yazar Mehmet Yaşin ve Teoman Hünal'la geziyoruz, yiyoruz, görüyoruz, öğreniyoruz. "Görevimiz Yemek" iki ustanın samimi, çekişmeli, eğlenceli sohbetiyle iştahınızı açacak. Türkiye'nin birçok yerinde göreceğimiz bu iki üstat gittikleri yerlerde yediklerini, içtiklerini kendi tarzlarına göre yorumluyorlar ve zaman zaman ayrı fikirlere düşüp birbirleriyle karşı karşıya geliyorlar. İki farklı tarzı barındıran ve her ikisi de alanının birer dehası olan Yaşin ve Hünal yemek için bulundukları mekanlarda, eğlenceli atışmalı sohbetin ortasına atıveriyorlar bizi. Ortam bazen kızışacak bazen samimi bir hal alacak bazen de eğlenceden dört köşe olacak. Aynı hikayeyi yaşayan iki kafadar gurmeye sizler de ekranlardan eşlik ederken büyük keyif alacak, esprili, nefis bir sohbetin tam ortasında bulacaksınız kendinizi. Bazen modern bazen otantik bir hale bürünecek olan program "Görevimiz Yemek" iki eski dostun birbirleriyle olan samimiyetinden doğan zevkli sataşmalarının olacağı bölümlerle ekranlarda olacak. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: İstanbul'un Edebiyat Haritası
programme.desc: Romanlara, öykülere, şiirlere ve tüm dünyadan yazarlara asırlar boyu ilham olmuş İstanbul, edebi açıdan zengin bir mirasa sahip.

programme.title: Bana Her Yer Mutfak S1 B12
programme.desc: Murat Pala, Türkiye'nin değişik yörelerine gidip, o topraklarda yetişen gıdalardan birbirinden lezzetli yemekler yapıyor. Üstelik yemekleri yaparken de bir mutfağa tıkılıp kalmıyor. Çünkü o'na her yer mutfak!

programme.title: Anadolu'nun Gölleri
programme.desc: Her biri kendi karakteriyle var olan, birçok canlının yaşamına dokunan göller Bafa'dan Van'a, Karagöl'den Sapanca'ya kadar tüm yönleriyle ekrana geliyor.

programme.title: Doğada Kal S1 B12
programme.desc: Doğayı keşfetmenin merakı, yeni yerler görmek ve yeni hikayeler yaşamanın heyecanı... Şehirden uzaklaşıp doğada daha çok vakit geçirmek isteyenler için kamp hayatının bütün detayları Gökhan Konaş rehberliğinde sizler için anlatılıyor.

programme.title: İstikamet Karadeniz S1 B10
programme.desc: Çocukluğundan beri tutkusu olan deniz ve balık konusunda bir ucu gastronomi, diğer ucu sanata dayanan keyifli bir sohbetle ondan öğreneceğimiz çok şey var.

programme.title: Türkiye Fotoğraf Rotaları S1/7
programme.desc: Nuri Çorbacıoğlu doğup büyüdüğü Çivril - Denizli'ye giderek ilk ustası ve hocası Mehmet Çakır ile buluşacak. Işıklı Gölü'nde doğal hayata dair fotoğraflar çekecekler.

programme.title: 3.2.1 Kayıt S1 B5
programme.desc: Ahmet Sesigürgil, kameranın ardındaki sanatı, bir sahnenin duygusunu ve kompozisyonunu nasıl belirlediğini anlatıyor.

programme.title: Başka Hayat Mümkün S2 B5
programme.desc: Sebepleri farklı olsa da ortak noktası yeni bir yaşam kurma isteğiydi. Nasıl karar verdiler? Neden gitmek istediler? Gitmeyi nasıl başardılar? Mutlular mı? Aradıklarını buldular mı? Başka bir hayat gerçekten mümkün mü? Başaran insanların zorlu hikayeleri...

programme.title: Duyulan Şehirler S1 B9
programme.desc: Türkiye'nin en güçlü radyo seslerinden biri Yasemin Şefik, şehirlerin özgün seslerini kaydediyor, ardından müzik dünyasının usta aranjörleriyle bir araya getirerek unutulmaz şarkılara dönüştürüyor.

programme.title: Limonata 65
programme.desc: Ayhan Sicimoglu ile Limonata, izleyicilerini her ay dünyanin baska bir ülkesinde, farkli bir kültüre davet ediyor.

programme.title: Dünyayı Kim Kurtaracak? S1 B5
programme.desc: Doğaya ve canlılara saygılı, bütüncül, atıksız ve sürdürülebilir bir yaşam hayaliyle buluşmuş iki arkadaşın "sıfır atık yolculuğu" ekrana geliyor.

programme.title: VRT NWS Pano
programme.desc: Kleurrijke doosjes. Aantrekkelijke smaken. Tjokvol nicotine. Nicotinezakjes, beter bekend als snus, mogen in ons land niet verkocht worden, maar zijn populair onder jongeren. Experten slaan alarm. 'Er is een nieuwe generatie zeer verslaafd aan het worden, net nu sigaretten stilaan verdwijnen', zegt professor Filip Lardon (UAntwerpen). VRT NWS PANO en Knack slaan de handen in elkaar en onderzoeken hoe de tabaksindustrie ondermeer nicotinezakjes promoot. Want ... de industrie verkoopt een heel andere boodschap: deze zakjes helpen rokers van hun sigaretten af. Zweden geldt daarbij als het grote voorbeeld, bijna niemand rookt nog, maar snus is er legaal op de markt, én alomtegenwoordig. Maar hoe krijgt de tabaksindustrie (of is het de nicotine-industrie?) die boodschap tot bij politici en het grote publiek? Pano en Knack onderzoeken ook de lobby achter de zakjes, net nu Europa de regels dreigt aan te scherpen. Reportage: Wim Van den Eynde en Jan Konings (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Flikken Maastricht
programme.desc: Het onderzoek naar de familie Vizee wordt groots aangepakt. De geldstromen worden in kaart gebracht en tijdens een huiszoeking bij de voetbalclub vinden ze het mogelijke wapen waarmee de twee chemici van het drugslab vermoord zijn. Ondertussen verschijnt Fleur ineens met haar nieuwe vriend in Maastricht. Ze blijkt op de een of andere manier betrokken bij de geldstromen van de familie Vizee. Reden genoeg voor Mechels om Wolfs en Eva van de zaak te halen. Maar daar blijkt ze te laat mee te zijn... (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Witse
programme.desc: Een lesbische vrouw, Lies, maakt ruzie met haar vriendin Anja, die haar bedriegt met een man. Later op de avond wordt Lies verdronken en geëlektrocuteerd teruggevonden in bad. programme.title: De laatste lach
programme.desc: Vijf mensen die ongeneeslijk ziek zijn kiezen voor de troost van de lach. Ze geven een humorist een bijzondere opdracht: schrijf een grafrede, maar dan wel eentje om te lachen. Om die afscheidsspeech te schrijven, moeten ze elkaar leren kennen. Philippe Geubels, Jade Mintjens, Janne Desmet, Otto Jan Ham en Pedro Elias duiken telkens in een leven vol verhalen om inspiratie op te doen voor hun tekst. Ze brengen elk op hun eigen manier een eerbetoon dat even persoonlijk als humoristisch is. Nog vóór de grafrede op hun uitvaart gebracht wordt, krijgen deze mensen zelf te horen wat er na hun dood over hen verteld zal worden. (Senderinfo).

programme.title: Over mijn lijf
programme.desc: Kobe Ilsen en Danira Boukhriss duiken in de wereld van slaap. Wat doet slaaptekort met ons lichaam, en hoe kunnen we onze slaap verbeteren? (Senderinfo).

programme.title: VRT NWS Pano
programme.desc: Kleurrijke doosjes. Aantrekkelijke smaken. Tjokvol nicotine. Nicotinezakjes, beter bekend als snus, mogen in ons land niet verkocht worden, maar zijn populair onder jongeren. Experten slaan alarm. 'Er is een nieuwe generatie zeer verslaafd aan het worden, net nu sigaretten stilaan verdwijnen', zegt professor Filip Lardon (UAntwerpen). VRT NWS PANO en Knack slaan de handen in elkaar en onderzoeken hoe de tabaksindustrie ondermeer nicotinezakjes promoot. Want ... de industrie verkoopt een heel andere boodschap: deze zakjes helpen rokers van hun sigaretten af. Zweden geldt daarbij als het grote voorbeeld, bijna niemand rookt nog, maar snus is er legaal op de markt, én alomtegenwoordig. Maar hoe krijgt de tabaksindustrie (of is het de nicotine-industrie?) die boodschap tot bij politici en het grote publiek? Pano en Knack onderzoeken ook de lobby achter de zakjes, net nu Europa de regels dreigt aan te scherpen. Reportage: Wim Van den Eynde en Jan Konings (Senderinfo).

programme.desc: Het is zomer en de tienjarige Yaren vertrekt op kamp. Ze is nerveus, want het is niet zomaar een kamp... En daar heeft ze het natuurlijk nog steeds moeilijk mee. Op dit rouwkamp botst Yaren op de enthousiaste spring-in-'t-veld Kato. programme.title: Wunderwelt Schweiz
programme.desc: Von der rauen Bergwelt der Tessiner Hochalpen bis ins liebliche Muggiotal im südlichsten Eck des Tessins: kaum ein anderer Kanton steckt so voller Kontraste. In kaum einer anderen Region der Schweiz sind Gegensätze so reizvoll wie im Tessin: Es ist die sonnigste aber gleichzeitig die regnerischste Region der Eidgenossenschaft. Schroffes Hochgebirge trifft auf mediterranes Klima und während im Norden noch Schnee liegt, blühen im Süden bereits Kamelien und Magnolien. Durch seine geographische Lage vereinen sich hier die unterschiedlichsten Klimazonen auf engstem Raum. Berühmt ist das Tessin für seine Seen. Die bekanntesten sind der Lago Maggiore und der Luganer See. Entstanden aus den Gletschern der Eiszeit, sind sie heute das Sinnbild für italienisches Dolce Vita Flair vor alpiner Kulisse und beliebte Touristenziele. Doch unweit der Piazzas und Promenaden findet sich wilde Natur. Sei es im Vogelparadies Bolle di Magadino oder im rauen Maggiatal. Noch vor gar nicht langer Zeit war das Tessin ein bitterarmer Kanton. Davon zeugen viele verlassenen Dörfer - besonders in den unzugänglichen Seitentälern der rauen Bergwelt. In manchen, wie dem Val Bavona, gibt es nur in einem Dorf Strom. Doch das Tessin ist schon immer reich an landschaftlicher Schönheit gewesen. Auf den Bergwiesen der Alpe Piora und Dötra liegen wahre Blumenmeere, in denen sich kleine Dramen um Leben und Tod abspielen. Vom Murmeltier zur Smaragdeidechse - auch die Tierwelt des Tessins ist bunt und abwechslungsreich und auf dem Monte Generoso begegnet man sogar mit etwas Glück Wildpferden. Der Film zeigt in farbenprächtigen Bildern die ganze Vielfalt des Tessins. Aufregende Tieraufnahmen, wie die berühmten Balztänze der Haubentaucher oder die Flugkünste der Rauchschwalben lassen den Zuschauer staunen und entführen ihn in eine der zauberhaftesten Regionen der Schweiz.

programme.title: Love of the Wild
programme.desc: S1 E2 — The Wilds of Russian KareliaIn der riesigen russischen Wildnis Kareliens verwaltet und schützt Viktor Iljin eines der größten Naturschutzgebiete Europas. Seine Expertise über das lokale Ökosystem und sein Engagement, es für zukünftige Generationen zu erhalten, machen diese Folge zu einer Reise in die verborgenen Tiefen der russischen Wildnis.

programme.title: Faszination Heimat
programme.desc: S1 E12 — Tatort AlmwieseDie Alpen zählen zu den wichtigsten Ökoregionen der Erde, denn ihre Natur und ihre Lebensräume sind enorm vielfältig. Ein neuer Blickwinkel auf die atemberaubende Landschaft bietet eine erstaunliche und ungewohnte Einsicht in die eigene Lebenswelt.

programme.title: Wunderwelt Schweiz
programme.desc: Diese Folge führt in eine vergleichsweise unbekannte Ecke der Schweiz: die Jura-Region. Eine Entdeckungsreise in eine fast unberührte Natur im Wechsel der Jahreszeiten. Das Juragebirge ist der kleine Bruder der Alpen. Es verläuft im Nordosten der Schweiz entlang der französischen Grenze. Im Vergleich zu den touristischen Hotspots der Schweiz ist das facettenreiche Mittelgebirge noch relativ unbekannt. Dabei gibt es hier viel zu entdecken. Der Jura scheint fast wie in einem Dornröschenschlaf. Während der Rest der Schweiz vergleichsweise dicht besiedelt ist, gibt es in der Jura-Region noch viel Platz für unberührte Natur. Vom Frühling im bunt blühenden Ajoie, dem Obstgarten der Nordostschweiz, über den Sommer im idyllischen Vallée de Joux bis hin zum bitterkalten Winter im kältesten Ort der Schweiz - das Jahr im Jura steckt voller Überraschungen. Wir begegnen Füchsen und Fledermäusen, und statten einer der größten Ameisenkolonien Europas einen Besuch ab. Sogar der Luchs ist mittlerweile ins Jura zurückgekehrt. Wir tauchen ab in die Erdgeschichte und erfahren, warum das Juragebirge zum Namensgeber einer ganzen Erdepoche wurde. Die Juraregion ist rau und lieblich zugleich. Die schroffen Kalkfelsen des Mittelgebirges sind dicht bewaldet und auf ihren Gipfeln finden sich bunt blühende Bergwiesen. Inmitten ragt der "Schweizer Grand Canyon" empor, der Creux du Van, ein einzigartiges Naturmonument, geschaffen durch Wasser, Eis und Zeit. Auf dem Hochplateau des Bezirks Franches-Montagnes begegnen wir den "Freibergern.

programme.title: Von Hirtinnen und Wölfen
programme.desc: Mitten in der rauen Schönheit der Berge trotzen einige moderne Hirten Wind, Wetter und dem Wolf. Dazu zählt auch die Hirtin Anna, die jeden Sommer mit ihren Schafen in die Einsamkeit der Berge zieht, sowie Jäger, Biobauern und Naturschützer.

programme.title: Bodensee - Wildnis am großen Wasser
programme.desc: Kultur, Wasser und Natur versprechen Besuchern aus ganz Europa Festspiele ganz besonderer Art. Doch auch abseits der Bühnen versammeln sich jedes Jahr unzählige Besucher, meist von weit her. Wie ein Magnet zieht der Bodensee Hunderttausende Zugvögel an. Der Film ist eine Reise über und unter Wasser und zu verborgenen Ufern - mit manchen Überraschungen, denn die Dreharbeiten erstreckten sich über alle vier Jahreszeiten, zu Tages- und Nachtzeit.

programme.desc: S1 E1 — FrühlingsgefühleDie Zoologin Gudrun Kaufmann und der Experte Prof. Walter Arnold begeben sich auf Spurensuche in der Natur. Sie erläutern faszinierende Phänomene – etwa, warum Wölfe zu Unrecht ein negatives Ansehen haben und weshalb Moorfrösche ihre Farbe ändern.

programme.title: Wildes Land
programme.desc: Naturjuwel Nationalpark KalkalpenIm Herbst ist der Nationalpark Kalkalpen in Oberösterreich ein farbenprächtiger Anblick. Hier hat sich die Natur grandiose Denkmäler geschaffen. Die schönsten Naturplätze im Nationalpark. Wenn die Tage kürzer werden, die Kraft der Sonne merklich nachlässt und die Laubfärbung einsetzt, zieht der Herbst ins Land. Eine faszinierende Jahreszeit, die ihre ganz eigenen Reize im Nationalpark offenbart. Hier ist der Mensch nur Gast, die Natur führt Regie.

programme.title: Love of the Wild

programme.desc: S2 E2 — Der EisbändigerDie Großglockner Hochalpenstraße ist am Ende des Winters unter meterhohem Schnee begraben. Zum 1. Mai muss sie geräumt sein. Die Eisbändiger sind nicht alleine im Kampf gegen die gewaltigen Schneemassen, denn ein zweites Team kommt zur Hilfe.

programme.title: Wunderwelt Schweiz
programme.desc: Graubünden im Winter, das heißt für viele Pistenspaß. In der Natur herrscht jedoch wegen der eisigen Kälte ein ständiger Kampf ums Überleben. Ob Steinbock oder Kreuzotter, sie alle haben Strategien, um in der Kälte des Winters zu überleben. Bei den Murmeltieren lautet die Strategie: Fett anfressen und die kalte Jahreszeit schlafend überstehen. Dieser Winterschlaf ist jedoch nicht mit dem erholsamen Schlaf in der Nacht zu vergleichen: Er ist vielmehr eine lebensbedrohliche Notsituation. Forscher haben herausgefunden: Wenn Murmeltiere nicht manchmal aus dem Winterschlaf erwachen, und "richtig" schlafen, dann sterben sie. Verblüffend auch die Überlebenstaktik der Steinböcke. Obwohl sie im Hochgebirge leben, scheinen sie keinen Schnee zu mögen, Sie gehen ihm aus dem Weg, wo immer sie können. In den kalten Winternächten sinkt zum Energiesparen ihre Körpertemperatur, in den Beinen auf bis zu 15 Grad. Was für andere Tiere den Tod durch Erfrieren bedeuten würde, ist für den Steinbock eine Fähigkeit, die ihm das Überleben sichert. Diese und andere erstaunliche Geschichten aus der winterlichen Natur erzählt der Film mit packenden Bildern einer grandiosen Natur und prächtigen Landschaftsaufnahmen. Mehrere Filmteams waren zu Lande, unter dem Eis und in der Luft unterwegs. Unter anderem wurde auch ein Cineflex-System eingesetzt, mit dem besonders ruhige Aufnahmen vom Helikopter aus gedreht werden können. Doch auch der härteste Winter ist irgendwann einmal zu Ende, und die Natur atmet auf. Dies wird am deutlichsten beim Anblick von Gämsen, die voller Lebensfreude mit verrückten Sprüngen die Ankunft des Frühlings zu feiern scheinen. Die Murmeltiere haben für so etwas keine Zeit. Ihr Sommer ist oft so kurz, dass die Männchen die noch schlafenden Weibchen begatten. Für sie sind Frühling und Sommer nichts anderes als Vorbereitungszeit für den nächsten Überlebenskampf im Graubündener Winter.

programme.title: Wildes Land
programme.desc: Naturjuwel Nationalpark KalkalpenIm Herbst ist der Nationalpark Kalkalpen in Oberösterreich ein farbenprächtiger Anblick. Hier hat sich die Natur grandiose Denkmäler geschaffen. Die schönsten Naturplätze im Nationalpark. Wenn die Tage kürzer werden, die Kraft der Sonne merklich nachlässt und die Laubfärbung einsetzt, zieht der Herbst ins Land. Eine faszinierende Jahreszeit, die ihre ganz eigenen Reize im Nationalpark offenbart. Hier ist der Mensch nur Gast, die Natur führt Regie.
